messages.subject: v1.2 branch and preview
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone, I just created a release branch for version 1.2, called v1.2. You can also read an introduction <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/rmr-v1.2-Preview> to the new release. Your feedback is welcome, but I need to warn you that only bug fixes and minor changes are possible at this stage. For v1.3 we hope to have a more open process where changes are discussed before they are implemented, when major changes are still possible. In  a way it's always been possible as almost any change and certainly important ones have associated issues in the github issue tracker, where you can add your comments, but I guess it's difficult to get the big picture from the tickets alone, and I've not been using milestones with the necessary zeal. More on v1.3 soon. And, by the way, welcome to our discussion group. I hope it will bring more of the conversations we've been having over email in the open. We are happy to reply to email, it's just that sharing our RHadoop problems and successes with the community multiplies the benefit of those conversations manyfold. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: rhbase, thrift serialization
messages.body_plain:
Antonio,

rhadoop is a great framework and thanks for getting it on github.

I have been using R for a while developing some machine learning algorithms. I have rhadoop setup, and am using hbase-thrift (bin/hbase thrift start) to get to hbase. What I see is that information is getting serialized in rhbase (R's default serialize function), but, it seems that it is not getting deserialized going through hbase-thrift.

When I scan a table while in the hbase shell, there is extra Hex code prepended to a key for a a row I inserted from R/rhbase using hb.insert, compared to if I inserted a row directly in hbase using ruby.

key should be: 1054412861,

but instead it is: X\x0A\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x02\x0D\x01\x00\x02\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x10\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x09\x00\x00\x00\x0A1054412861

Do you recognize this problem that I am having?

I wonder if I have to: 1) enable thrift to deserialize 2) start up thrift a different way 3) disable serialization in rhbase, or use a different serializer.

I started to dive into the R code supporting rhbase, it is starting to make sense to me. Maybe I can help out sometime in the future ;-).

Thanks,

Owen

messages.subject: Re: rhbase, thrift serialization
messages.body_plain:
What is happening, I believe, is that rhbase uses the default R serialization. There is no implementation outside R of that serialization and hbase sees just the raw bytes. We would need a thrift implementation in R to be able to do what you want, I think that's your proposal number 3. Also take a look at typedbytes (HADOOP-1722) and see if that can help (we have an R serde implementation for that). Once you have that the major rhbase calls are parametrized w.r.t. serde.

Antonio

> Do you recognize this problem that I am having?

Hi Owen,

  I had exactly the same problem. As Antonio says, this Hex code is
added by R during serialization. HBase is not able to unserialize R
objects on the other hand.

The solution I used is 3): as a test, add parameters sz=charToRaw,
usz=rawToChar and try to write strings only. ^^

I wrote more code to be able to encode more types and read them from
Java, but except for the Java long issue, Antonio did it better within
his typed.bytes implementation. The problem raised after is that you
need to know the types of the objects you put into HBase.

--
Xavier

On 02/23/2012 01:40 PM, Owen McCusker wrote:

> I have been using R for a while developing some machine learning

> thrift start) to get to hbase. What I see is that information is getting
> serialized in rhbase (R's default serialize function), but, it seems
> that it is not getting deserialized going through hbase-thrift.

hbase-thrift does not do serialization. "hbase shell" does only "string"
unserialization when you read (from the shell) and... that's all. Even
if you write from Java, the float which is encoded cannot be read
through hbase shell.

--
Xavier

messages.subject: rbase and filter handling
messages.body_plain:
I passed in some filter commands e.g. { LIMIT=>2 },  to hb.scan and there was no effect.

So I used tcpdump to dump the packet payloads going to the hbase/thrift server. I could see that the filter command was not getting included in the payload to the thrift server. So it looks like this is there as a future hook, or maybe I used it incorrectly. It could be that the supporting API call, hbScannerOpenFilter, could does not process the argument yet.

I also started to look into filter support through the openScanner Hbase/Thrift API. It looks like it is not there yet.

http://wiki.apache.org/hadoop/Hbase/ThriftApi

But, I did start to track new development in customer filters via the Thrift Interface.

https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HBASE-5428, schedule for Hbase release 0.94.0. I currently working with hbase version 0.90.4 on my Mac OS X development box.

--

Owen

Please do not hesitate with comments and suggestions.
